concepts.why: Secular scholar / all readers: the name says 'rested on them, and they prophesied', but Numbers 24:2 as quoted says only that the Spirit of God came upon Balaam; the verse does not say he prophesied (his oracle begins in v.3, outside the passage). Drop it, or extend to Numbers 24:2-3 and re-check that v.3 carries speaking. 2 Chronicles 24:20 and Ezekiel 11:5 also lack the word 'prophesied' but plainly give the Spirit's message ('This is what God says', 'declare that this is what the LORD says'), so they may stay.

Baptist/dispensational, Reformed, Jewish readers of the Hebrew Bible, secular scholar: 2 Corinthians 3:3 never says 'new spirit'. It says the Spirit writes on 'tablets of human hearts' not 'tablets of stone', and set as the closing line under Ezekiel 11:19 / 36:26 ('heart of stone ... heart of flesh') it reads as Paul fulfilling Ezekiel, which is exactly where the traditions part (new covenant vs. Israel's promise). It also fails 'holds the concept, not merely shares a word'. Move it to concept 38 (Not of the letter but of the Spirit), where it sits beside 2 Cor 3:6, 3:8 and says what it says (38 would then have 5 passages).

concepts.name: The Spirit poured out
concepts.why: Baptist/dispensational, Jewish-reader/secular, Reformed: the name 'I will pour out My Spirit' is a future-tense promise (Isaiah, Ezekiel, Joel, Zechariah), and four of the eight passages beneath it (Acts 2:16-17, 2:33, 10:45, Titus 3:6) are past-tense NT statements. Under that name the grouping itself says the NT events are the promise being kept, the very claim the site must not make, and dispensationalists in particular part on whether Pentecost fulfils Joel. Concept 13 was kept Isaiah-only for this reason; 15 should be neutral in the same way. A plain label in the verb all eight share ('poured out') leaves Acts 2:16's own 'this is what was spoken by the prophet Joel' as the text's claim, not the site's. Passages and notes unchanged.

concepts.name: Through the spirit: declared, offered, vindicated, made alive
concepts.why: Name against passages: 'vindicated' is 1 Timothy 3:16 alone and 'made alive' is 1 Peter 3:18 alone. Romans 1:4 says 'declared ... through the Spirit of holiness' and Hebrews 9:14 says 'offered Himself ... through the eternal Spirit'; neither says vindicated or made alive, so a name carrying only those two verbs says more than half its passages. The four-verb name uses each passage's own verb and keeps the lower-case 'spirit' for the reason the drafter gives (readers part on whether each verse names the Holy Spirit). Secular/Jewish reader: no change to passages. Alternative if shorter wanted: 'Through the Spirit of holiness, through the eternal Spirit'.

note_fixes: Mark 13:11: the verse says nothing of witnessing or testifying (it says what to say when handed over; it is the same saying as Matthew 10:20 in concept 6). Either extend the passage to Mark 13:9-11 only if the verses there carry 'witness'/'testimony' in the Berean, or move Mark 13:11 beside Matthew 10:20 (concept 6 is at 8 passages, so one of its weaker Old Testament or Mark 12:36 lines would have to go, or leave it here and accept it as the 'when they hand you over' pair to Luke 12:12 in concept 25).
concepts.why: All readers: three renderings of one saying (Matthew 10:20, Mark 13:11, Luke 12:12) sit in three different concepts, and Mark 13:11 is the one whose placement the name ('You will be My witnesses') does not support. 1 Thessalonians 1:5 is thin (gospel came 'in the Holy Spirit') but holds the preaching sense and may stay.

concepts.name: Each of you should use whatever gift he has received
concepts.why: Secular scholar and all readers: this concept is a Spirit-theme concept in which no passage names the Spirit (the drafter says so), under a name ('Different gifts according to the grace given us') that repeats the previous concept's 'Different gifts' almost word for word. As it stands a reader of the Spirit theme cannot tell the two apart and is told by position that Romans 12, Ephesians 4 and 1 Peter 4 are gifts of the Spirit, which the verses do not say. Rename it from 1 Peter 4:10 (or Ephesians 4:11, 'He gave some to be apostles ...') so the two read as 'gifts the Spirit apportions' and 'gifts received and used', and consider whether it belongs in the Spirit outline at all rather than in Church; if kept, keep it as the texts' words only.

note_fixes: 1 Corinthians 13:8: the Berean's 'they will be restrained' renders a verb the original gives as 'cease' (MACULA: paysontai, the middle of pauo); the packet records the gap. Baptist/Reformed (cessationist) and secular readers will see a note that rests on one translation's softening of the very verse the debate turns on, and Pentecostal readers will see it favoured. The original arbitrates: trim the note to 'Love never fails. But where there are prophecies, they will cease', which is still an exact quotation and avoids the contested clause; the verse is shown whole beneath it.
concepts.why: The grouping itself is fair (12:30, 13:8, 14:19, 14:22 beside 14:4, 14:5, 14:18, 14:39 gives both sides). Only the 13:8 note is the problem.

concepts.name: Worship in spirit and truth; pray in the Spirit
concepts.why: Secular scholar, Reformed, Catholic, Orthodox: the name capitalises 'Spirit' across the board, but John 4:24 reads 'worship Him in spirit and in truth' in lower case in the Berean, and whether that is the Holy Spirit or the human spirit is a point where readers part (the drafter applies lower-case for this reason in concepts 3, 19 and 31). A capital in the name takes the first reading for John 4:24. The two-part name uses each passage's own case: John 4:24 for worship, Ephesians 6:18 and Jude 1:20 for prayer in the (Holy) Spirit; Romans 8:26-27 stays with prayer.

secondary_or_links: SAME SUB-THEME NAMED TWICE: 32 'Different gifts, the same Spirit' and 33 'Different gifts according to the grace given us'. Both are the gifts of 1 Corinthians 12 (12:28-31 in 33 is the same chapter as 12:4-11 in 32); the split exists only for the 8-passage bound. At minimum rename 33 as suggested; better, fold the Spirit-naming lines into 32 and move the rest to Church.

SAME SUB-THEME NAMED TWICE: 6 'The Spirit spoke through me' and 53 'What the Spirit says'. Mark 12:36, Acts 4:25 and Acts 28:25 (the Spirit speaking in scripture) are the same thing as Hebrews 3:7 and 10:15 (the Holy Spirit says, quoting scripture); the difference is only tense and the Revelation / Agabus lines. If kept apart, move Hebrews 3:7 and 10:15 into 6 and let 53 hold Revelation 2:7, 14:13, 1 Timothy 4:1, Acts 11:28, 21:11 (5 passages).

SAME SUB-THEME NAMED TWICE: 31 'The Spirit directing the way' and 42 'Led by the Spirit'. Acts 16:6, 20:22 (compelled by the Spirit) and Acts 8:29 are the Spirit leading, as are Matthew 4:1, Romans 8:14 and Galatians 5:18; 41 'Walk by the Spirit' sits very close on Galatians 5:16 / 5:18. Consider merging 31 and 42 (14 passages exceeds the bound, so keep the split but name them apart, e.g. 31 by Acts 13:2 'The Holy Spirit said'; 42 stays as is).

Weaker pair: 34 'They spoke in tongues' and 35 'Tongues and prophecy', split by the drafter only to stay under the passage bound; the Acts and 1 Corinthians halves are defensible as two (event vs. regulation) and are not a fault if named as they are.

Order and the 'no Old Testament under a New Testament name' rule: 54 (closing hope) carries Isaiah 32:15 and 59:21 beneath Romans 15:13's name. The name is a wish, not a claim of fulfilment, and the closing concept needs the dark and the hope together, so no change is needed; noted only because concept 13 was built Isaiah-only on this rule.

Concept 21 (Baptized with the Holy Spirit) accepted: the Berean varies 'with' and 'in', but the original has the same preposition (en) in Mark 1:8, Luke 3:16, John 1:33, Acts 1:5, 11:16 and 1 Cor 12:13, so putting 1 Cor 12:13 beside the Gospels takes no side the Greek does not.

Concept 12 (Matthew 3:11-12 under 'a spirit of judgment and a spirit of fire') accepted: the passage itself runs from the Spirit and fire into the winnowing and unquenchable fire, so the grouping follows the verse, and Luke 3:16 (without the winnowing) stands separately in 21.
Secondary: no changes. Links: no changes (no Baptism theme exists; 'Father, Son and Holy Spirit' is present).
